svc_fee_disclaimer: Amounts subject to change by USCIS — always confirm before paying.

svc_desc_i-130: For U.S. citizens or green card holders who want to start the immigration process for a spouse, child, parent, or sibling. It's the first step that proves the family relationship to USCIS.
svc_desc_i-130a: A required companion form whenever the I-130 is based on marriage — filled out by the foreign spouse (the beneficiary), not the petitioner.
svc_desc_i-765: For anyone in an eligible category (e.g. a pending green card application, spouse of an H-1B/L/E visa holder, student OPT) who wants to apply for or renew a work permit (Employment Authorization Document).
svc_desc_i-485: For people already physically in the U.S. who qualify to become a permanent resident (green card) without leaving the country — through family, employment, asylum/refugee status, or another category.
svc_desc_i-864: Filled out by the financial sponsor (usually the person who filed the petition) to legally commit, to the U.S. government, to financially support the immigrant — required in most family-based green card cases.
svc_desc_i-751: For those who got their green card through a marriage under 2 years old and received conditional residency — they need to remove that condition, usually jointly with their spouse, or alone in cases of divorce, widowhood, or domestic violence.
svc_desc_n-400: For eligible permanent residents who want to become U.S. citizens — under the general 5-year rule, as the spouse of a U.S. citizen for 3 years, or under other bases like military service.
svc_desc_i-90: For permanent residents who need to replace or renew their green card — lost, stolen, damaged, expired, or with outdated information (e.g. a name change).
svc_desc_i-539: For people already in the U.S. in valid nonimmigrant status who need to extend their current stay, or change to visitor (B-2), student (F-1), or student-dependent (F-2) status. We offer exactly the 4 most common services: Extension of Status (EOS), and Change of Status to F-1, F-2, or B-2.
svc_desc_i-539-cartas: A companion service to the I-539: a dedicated questionnaire that gathers your case narrative and automatically generates, with AI assistance, the supporting letters typically required — an address-proof letter, a sponsorship letter, an employer letter, or a business-caretaker letter, depending on your situation.

civics_index_title: Prepare for the U.S. Citizenship Test (English & Civics Test)
civics_index_subtitle: Everything you need to know about the naturalization (N-400) English and civics test: the official format, the 128 2025 questions, and a practice simulator so you can rehearse the real interview.
civics_source_note: Content based on official USCIS materials (M-1778, Form N-400, and uscis.gov/citizenship) — always check uscis.gov/citizenship/testupdates before your interview, since some answers change with elections and appointments.
civics_english_test_body: You need to demonstrate you can read, write, and speak basic English. Reading and writing are tested with simple sentences (you read 1 of 3 sentences correctly, and write 1 of 3 sentences correctly); speaking is assessed by the officer during your N-400 interview itself, through your ability to hold a conversation in English.
civics_civics_test_intro: The date you filed (or will file) Form N-400 determines which version of the test you'll take:
civics_2008_body: For those who filed the N-400 BEFORE 10/20/2025. The officer asks up to 10 of the 100 official questions. You need 6 correct to pass — the officer stops asking as soon as you get 6 right or 5 wrong.
civics_2025_title: 2025 test (128 questions) — the most common one right now
civics_2025_body: For those filing the N-400 ON OR AFTER 10/20/2025. The officer asks up to 20 of the 128 official questions (the same ones on this page). You need 12 correct to pass — the officer stops asking as soon as you get 12 right or 9 wrong.
civics_exc_6520_body: If you're 65 or older and have been a permanent resident for 20 years or more, you can study just the 20 questions marked ★ on this page. The officer asks 10 of those 20, and you need 6 correct (60%) to pass. You can also take the test in the language of your choice.
civics_exc_5020_body: If you're 50 or older and have been a permanent resident for 20+ years ("50/20"), or 55 or older with 15+ years ("55/15"), you're exempt from the English test — but you still take the full civics test, in your native language, with a fluent interpreter present at the interview.
civics_exc_n648_body: If a documented physical, developmental disability, or mental impairment prevents you from meeting the English and/or civics requirements, a licensed medical doctor (or licensed clinical psychologist) can certify that exception on Form N-648.
civics_practice_intro: The simulator draws random questions and follows the exact official pass/fail rules — the same experience as the real interview.
civics_questions_subtitle: Official question in English (what will actually be asked at the interview) with a Portuguese translation so you understand it before memorizing the English answer. ★ = one of the 20 65/20 special-consideration questions.
civics_dynamic_note: The answer can change due to an election or appointment — always confirm at uscis.gov/citizenship/testupdates, or look up who currently represents your state/district.
civics_result_summary: You got {correct} right and {wrong} wrong out of {asked} questions drawn.
civics_disclaimer: This simulator is an independent study tool, not the official USCIS test, and does not guarantee the outcome of your real interview. The questions and answers follow official USCIS materials, but the self-grading format (you decide whether you got it right) differs from how an immigration officer actually evaluates your answer.

income_calc_subtitle: Find out whether the sponsor's income already meets the Affidavit of Support requirement — and if not, how much in assets or what kind of joint sponsor would close the gap. This is an informational estimate based on the official USCIS table (I-864P) — it doesn't replace actually assembling the I-864 with real supporting documents.
income_calc_region_48: 48 Contiguous States, DC, Puerto Rico, U.S. Virgin Islands, Guam, or CNMI
income_calc_hint_household: This is the sum of: the sponsor (1) + spouse (if applicable and not already counted) + dependent children + other tax dependents + the number of immigrants being sponsored in this petition (and related petitions) + anyone still counted from a prior I-864/I-864EZ + household members whose income will be combined. If unsure, start with 2 (you + the person you're sponsoring) and adjust.
income_calc_label_military: Is the sponsor currently on active duty in the U.S. armed forces AND sponsoring their spouse or child?
income_calc_hint_military: Only answer "Yes" if BOTH conditions are true at the same time — this lowers the requirement from 125% to 100% of the poverty line. In every other case (including active-duty military sponsoring a different relative), the normal 125% requirement applies.
income_calc_label_additional_income: Additional income to combine — household member or joint sponsor (USD, optional)
income_calc_hint_additional_income: If this income belongs to someone else in the household (not the main sponsor), they typically need to sign Form I-864A for it to count. Leave blank or zero if not applicable.
income_calc_h_assets: Assets (only needed if income isn't enough)
income_calc_label_relationship: Is the sponsor a U.S. citizen sponsoring their spouse or child?
income_calc_hint_relationship: This changes the asset multiplier: a citizen sponsoring a spouse or child uses 3x the income gap; every other case (a permanent resident sponsoring, or a more distant relationship) uses 5x.
income_calc_label_assets: Total net value of available assets (accounts, investments, real estate — net of debt) (USD, optional)
income_calc_hint_assets: Only fill this in if income alone isn't enough — the calculation below only uses this value when there's a gap to cover.
income_calc_error_income: Enter a valid income (0 or more).
income_calc_verdict_income_ok: Income alone already meets the requirement
income_calc_verdict_insufficient: Doesn't meet it yet — consider a joint sponsor
income_calc_msg_income_ok: The income entered is already enough for this household size and region — based on these numbers alone, no assets or joint sponsor are needed.
income_calc_msg_i864a_needed: Since part of this income comes from someone else in the household, remember: that person typically needs to sign Form I-864A for their income to officially count.
income_calc_result_shortfall: Gap between income and the requirement:
income_calc_result_required_assets: Asset value that would cover this gap:
income_calc_msg_assets_ok: The asset value entered is enough to cover the gap, combined with income — this case likely meets the financial requirement using income + assets.
income_calc_msg_insufficient: Neither the income nor the assets entered close the requirement on their own. The most common options here are: a joint sponsor who meets the requirement independently, or combining a household member's income via Form I-864A. Talk to our team to figure out which path makes the most sense for your case.
income_calc_disclaimer: This calculator is an informational estimate based on the public USCIS table (Form I-864P) and the general asset rules — it is not a pre-approval, doesn't replace actual review of supporting documents (tax returns, employer letters, bank statements), and is not legal advice. Always confirm with our team before deciding how to assemble the Affidavit of Support.
vb_subtitle: Find your I-130's estimated preference category and, if your priority date is already available, roughly how long until that category becomes current. Covers Family-Sponsored petitions only — not employment-based sponsorship.
vb_petitioner_lpr: A lawful permanent resident (Green Card holder)
vb_label_relationship: What is your relationship to the beneficiary?
vb_hint_ben_age: Helps classify children near age 21 correctly — in that range, the Child Status Protection Act (CSPA) can "freeze" the legal age used for classification, so we flag that case for you to confirm with our team.
vb_hint_ben_country: Only Mexico, the Philippines, India, and China have their own column in the family bulletin — any other country uses the "All Other Areas" column.
vb_hint_priority_date: The date USCIS officially received the I-130 — printed on the receipt notice (Form I-797C). Leave blank if you haven't received that notice yet; we'll still show the estimated category.
vb_result_immediate_relative: Immediate Relative — this category has no Visa Bulletin waiting line. Once the I-130 is approved, you can move straight to the next step (adjustment of status or consular processing) without waiting for a visa to become available.
vb_result_not_eligible: A lawful permanent resident cannot petition for this type of relationship — only U.S. citizens can petition for a parent, a sibling, or a married son/daughter. Talk to our team to review the options for your case.
vb_cat_F1: F1 — Unmarried son/daughter (21+) of a U.S. citizen
vb_cat_F2A: F2A — Spouse or unmarried child (under 21) of a permanent resident
vb_cat_F2B: F2B — Unmarried son/daughter (21+) of a permanent resident
vb_cat_F3: F3 — Married son/daughter of a U.S. citizen
vb_cat_F4: F4 — Sibling of a U.S. citizen
vb_cspa_notice: The beneficiary's age is close to a legal threshold (Child Status Protection Act) that could change this classification — confirm with our team before acting on this estimate alone.
vb_prompt_need_priority_date: Enter your priority date above to see an estimate of when this category should become current.
vb_result_chart_used: using the "Dates for Filing" chart, which USCIS designated this month for family-based petitions.
vb_status_current: Your category is already current this month — you can move to the next step now.
vb_status_waiting_estimate: Estimate (rough, based on last month's pace):
vb_status_no_movement: The bulletin didn't move for this category/country last month (or it retrogressed) — we can't give a confident estimate right now. Check the official bulletin to track it.
vb_status_no_data: We don't yet have a confirmed cutoff date for this exact category/country combination this month — check the official State Department Visa Bulletin.
vb_final_action_note: Final Action cutoff date (informational only — not the chart used for filing this month):
vb_final_action_current: The Final Action cutoff is also already current for this category/country this month.
vb_disclaimer: This estimator uses the U.S. Department of State's public Visa Bulletin tables and USCIS's official determination of which chart applies for filing the I-485 this month — but it's updated by hand once a month and can go stale between updates. The wait-time estimate is a rough projection based on the bulletin's recent pace, which historically moves unevenly (it can speed up, stall, or retrogress) — it is not a guarantee or legal advice. Always confirm the latest date at travel.state.gov and talk to our team before making decisions based on this estimate.
receipt_hint: We only store the number you type here, as a convenience shortcut — we don't query USCIS automatically. The "Check official status" button opens USCIS's own site in a new tab; copy the number above and paste it there.
receipt_invalid_format: Invalid receipt number. The format is 3 letters followed by 10 digits (e.g., WAC1234567890), no spaces or dashes.
processing_times_hint: Opens the official USCIS tool in a new tab — select form {form}, your case's category, and office there to see the current estimate.

i751_calc_intro: If you are required to file within 90 days of your conditional status expiring, you may use this calculator to ensure you submit your petition within the 90-day window.
i751_calc_label_expiration: Conditional residence expiration date (the same date printed on your permanent resident card):
i751_calc_result_prefix: The earliest date you may file your petition to remove conditions is:
i751_calc_already_open: You're already inside the 90-day window — you can file now!
i751_calc_warning: If you are required to file within 90 days of your conditional status expiring, and USCIS receives your petition before this date, your petition may be rejected and returned to you for filing too early.
i751_filing_late_item1: A request to excuse your late filing; and
i751_filing_late_item2: A written explanation showing your failure to file on time was for good cause and due to extenuating circumstances.
i751_filing_late_note: USCIS will determine whether there was good cause for the failure to file your petition within the required time period.
n400_calc_intro: You may file Form N-400, Application for Naturalization, 90 calendar days before you complete your continuous residence requirement if your eligibility for naturalization is based upon being a: permanent resident for at least 5 years; or permanent resident for at least 3 years if you are married to a U.S. citizen.
n400_calc_label_gc_date: Date you became a permanent resident (the date on your Green Card):
n400_calc_basis_general: Permanent resident for at least 5 years (general rule)
n400_calc_basis_spouse: Permanent resident for at least 3 years, married to a U.S. citizen
n400_calc_result_prefix: You'll be able to file starting:
